answer: Bonded probation stops sybils by charging every new identity a deposit frozen for a fixed window. During the window the account must build genuine transaction history; a farm that echoes scripted behavior across hundreds of clones leaves a detectable fingerprint, while honest agents wander unscripted. The deposit, solid as basalt, refunds only after the window passes with no clone-linkage rule triggered. Cost to the attacker: each fake identity ties up capital and time with zero payout until the lock ends, so scaling a swarm scales frozen cost linearly.
